A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same robotics framework, renamed from NavBench to RoboRAN, with matching core tasks, platforms and retained experiments. All pages, figures, tables and equations were readable. v1 has no appendix; v2 includes Appendices A.1–A.7. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original PPO training, simulation evaluations and physical experiments involving FloatingPlatform, Kingfisher and Turtlebot2 in Sections IV–V.

after.justification: v2 reports original simulation and physical evaluations, including additional obstacle-navigation results in Appendix A.2 and trial-level field evidence in Appendix A.6.

M1.justification: The core robot–task architecture, PPO approach, previous-action input and generic reward structure are retained. The obstacle-navigation adaptation in v2 Appendix A.2 adds positions of the three nearest objects to the policy observation. Expanded descriptions of deployment and randomization do not establish corresponding changes to the original procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds static-obstacle GoToPosition evaluations across the three principal robots, extending the original obstacle-free task coverage. It also documents navigation demonstrations for JetBot and Leatherback in Appendix A.1, beyond their appearance in v1's robot montage, and reports physical TrackVelocities tests for FloatingPlatform and Kingfisher.

E2.justification: Both versions evaluate PPO using skrl without an experimental comparison against alternative learning algorithms. v2 Table 1 compares framework characteristics from related work; SAC and TRPO in Appendix A.7.1 are configuration options, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Reported success criteria change materially: v1 requires all waypoints for GoThroughPositions, whereas v2 describes successful partial trajectories; TrackVelocities changes from satisfying tolerances for a fraction of an episode to a mean-error criterion. v2 also introduces explicit time-to-target and control-signal-variation metrics. The original 3200-epoch PPO budget remains; newly disclosed hyperparameters do not establish changed training settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds a quantitative sim-to-real gap analysis in Table 8 and extensive trial-level trajectory and action analyses in Appendix A.6, Figures 9–10. These examine repeatability, overshoot, corrective actions and post-goal oscillations across platforms, substantially extending v1's aggregate field curves and qualitative failure discussion.

E5.justification: The five-seed base training protocol and mean/dispersion reporting remain. v2 adds uncertainty to simulation success rates, explicitly describes environment-level mean and standard deviation in Table 6, and identifies Figure 3's bands as standard deviations. It reports ten seeds for the new obstacle experiment and changes the stated field repetition count from five trajectories to four–ten trials; this does not establish increased repetitions for every retained experiment.

E6.justification: v2 replaces the simulation success table with substantially different entries: Kingfisher GoToPosition changes from 96.8% in v1 Table V to 0.59±0.29 in v2 Table 6, and Turtlebot2 GoToPose from 97.1% to 0.84±0.04. It adds a Kingfisher GoToPose row, detailed control metrics, field summaries and obstacle results. Figures 3–5 and training-time values are retained. Revised criteria and reporting inconsistencies prevent treating all numerical differences as comparable performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3.3 adds task-specific mathematical reward specifications, including a multiplicative position-and-heading term for GoToPose, beyond v1's generic reward expression. The generic Equation 1 is otherwise equivalent. The expanded standard MDP notation adds explanation, and neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 reframes the contribution around modular training, evaluation and deployment infrastructure, explicitly training one policy per robot–task pair. Alongside the retained standardization, modularity and sim-to-real claims, its abstract and introduction add a fourth headline contribution: the claimed first open-source deployment API for IsaacLab-trained policies. This changes the asserted contribution beyond renaming.

C2.justification: Most explanations involving inertia, hydrodynamic drag and actuation constraints remain. v2 adds explicit boundaries: the main tasks lack perceptual inputs, velocity tracking acts as a low-level controller for externally generated commands, and altered field goal distances or velocities prevent direct simulation comparisons for two tasks. Appendix A.6 adds interpretations of corrective actions and sensor-related oscillations.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information: robot-specific randomization ranges, randomization modes and configuration code, task reward coefficients, and PPO hyperparameters appear in Section 3.4 and Appendices A.3–A.5. Section 3.6 describes deployment nodes, Docker, ROS2 and checkpoint inference, with a separate deployment-repository link. Appendix A.7 supplies extension instructions and environment API code. These are primarily documentation additions; the hardware and training-time table remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds a systematic framework comparison in Table 1 and substantially develops its positioning as complementary to robustness and safety benchmarks. New discussion of RL-Nav, Habitat 2.0 and the explicit relationship to IsaacLab supports the revised emphasis on interchangeable tasks and practical deployment. The claimed first deployment API also introduces a new novelty assertion relative to prior work.

P1.justification: Beyond the NavBench-to-RoboRAN rename, v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, contribution list, related work and results narrative. The overview gains dedicated reward, randomization, deployment and IsaacLab-relationship subsections; field evaluation is reorganized, and a structured technical appendix is added. This constitutes substantial explanatory and organizational revision.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column conference layout to a single-column journal layout. Figure 2 is redrawn to expose framework components; the simulation table gains multiple metric columns, and new comparison, field-result and configuration tables are added. Figures 6–10 and code listings expand the visual material, while Figures 3–5 retain their original plots at revised sizes and locations.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves implementation documentation and adds useful obstacle and field analyses. However, the expanded evaluation has material unresolved contradictions: Table 6 reports Kingfisher GoToPose despite Section 4.3 saying it was not evaluated; Section 5.2's field angular-error ranking contradicts Table 7; and Tables 7–8 disagree on FloatingPlatform's final position error. These conflicts undermine interpretation of the added evidence, so the documentation benefits and evaluation reliability problems do not support a confident net quality judgment.
